title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: Rational design of lanthanide clusters remains difficult because the product is highly sensitive to the starting materials and to metal/ligand ratio, pH, solvent, temperature and time; the authors therefore prioritize assembly-mechanism studies and, separately, structure–property work that this review does not cover.
explanation: Both the strategy section and the conclusions state that cluster growth requires deliberate choice of hydrolysis-limiting ligands, metal sources, anion templates and those reaction variables. Future work is directed at the assembly mechanism and at combined theoretical and experimental property studies so that structure can eventually be designed from function and the reaction from the target structure.
scope: Synthetic lanthanide-cluster chemistry as framed by this review, especially high-nuclearity hydroxide clusters.
conditions: Sensitive variables named by the authors: metal ion/ligand ratio, pH, solvent, temperature and duration, plus identity of the starting materials.
caveats: Structure–property relationships, including SMM and magnetocaloric behavior mentioned only as motivation in the introduction, are explicitly outside the review’s analysis.
